column12: COMPOUND SLOW-RELEASE IMPLANT OF NALTREXONE AND RISPERIDONE, PREPARATION METHOD THEREFOR, AND USE THEREOF
column13: Disclosed is a compound sustained release implant of naltrexone and risperidone, and a preparation method and application thereof, which belong to the technical field of implant preparation. The naltrexone compound sustained-release implant includes naltrexone, risperidone, a degradable material A, a degradable material B, an additive and a lubricant. By controlling a mass ratio of naltrexone to risperidone to be (20-30):1, a weight-average molecular weight of the degradable material A to be 10-15W, and a weight-average molecular weight of the degradable material B in risperidone microspheres to be 2W-4W, the compound sustained release implant of naltrexone and risperidone can not only effectively inhibit amphetamine type drug relapse and reduce side effects of risperidone, but also realize the synchronous release of naltrexone and risperidone.

column12: LONG-ACTING SUSTAINED-RELEASE PREPARATION CONTAINING PRAMIPEXOLE AND PREPARATION METHOD THEREFOR
column13: Disclosed is a long-acting sustained-release preparation pharmaceutical composition containing pramipexole, comprising a pharmaceutically acceptable salt of pramipexole and a pharmaceutical high polymer material. The preparation is selected from a microsphere, a sustained-release particle, and a subcutaneous implant. The pharmaceutically acceptable salt of pramipexole is selected from erucate, stearate, oleate, α-linolenate, heptadecanoate, pamoate, and palmitate. The high polymer material is selected from PLGA, PLA, mPEG-PLA, and PEG-PLA-PEG. The present invention belongs to the technical field of pharmaceutical preparations and solves the problems of short release period and poor release effect of pramipexole in the prior art.

column12: MEDICAL SYSTEMS FOR TREATING CONDITIONS AND DISEASES OF THE PATIENT'S BODY CAVITIES
column13: The present invention provides methods and systems for treating conditions and diseases of a patient's body cavities, including urinary incontinence, transitional cell carcinoma, and other conditions. In particular, the present invention describes a drug delivery system for controlled delivery of drugs to body cavities of a patient, and the use of this system for treatment of the body cavities of the patient, for example, intravesical treatment. Many medications prescribed to patients with urinary tract diseases act locally. In many cases, such medications are administered orally or intravenously and spread through the digestive tract and bloodstream throughout the body, thereby affecting other body systems such as the immune system, kidneys, or liver and causing problematic adverse reactions. For local treatment, the present invention applies the drug directly to the cavity in a minimally invasive procedure.

column13: The invention discloses a composite microbial enzyme preparation and a preparation method thereof, and belongs to the technical field of bioplastic degradation. The enzyme preparation is synergistically constructed through a temperature-sensitive MOFs/Schiff base network composite carrier and black phosphorus quantum dots, FeO (at) ZIF-8 is taken as a core, and PNIPAM is grafted on the surface to form temperature-responsive MOFs; constructing a three-dimensional network carrier through Schiff base crosslinking of the CMC and the CNF; the complex enzyme is loaded on MOFs pore channels and then is embedded in a carrier network together with the black phosphorus quantum dots. The temperature-sensitive MOFs open pore channels to release enzyme when the compost is heated, and the Schiff base network dissociates secondary released enzyme under an acidic condition; the black phosphorus quantum dots promote enzyme activity and strengthen carrier response through a photothermal effect; the compound enzyme contains cutinase, alkaline lipase, neutral lipase, alpha-amylase, saccharifying enzyme, cellulase, laccase and protease, and can synergistically degrade PLA, PBAT and starch-based plastic. According to the invention, dual environment response controlled release, photo-thermal synergistic catalysis and synergistic degradation of the enzyme preparation are realized, and the plastic degradation period is shortened under the composting condition.

column12: SPECIFIC T CELL FOR PREVENTING OR TREATING CANCER, AND PREPARATION METHOD THEREFOR
column13: The present disclosure relates to a method for preparing a cancer-specific T cell based on peripheral blood or a peripheral immune organ for preventing or treating cancer, specifically including steps of: first, isolating an immune cell from peripheral blood or the peripheral immune organ; then, co-incubating with a nanoparticle and/or a microparticle loaded with a tumor whole-cell antigen for a period of time to activate the cancer-specific T cell; then, isolating a cancer-specific T cell activated by the tumor antigen; and, reinfusing the cancer-specific T cell into the body to exert an anti-cancer effect after in vitro expansion. According to the nanoparticle or microparticle prepared by the present disclosure, a tumor antigen component is loaded onto the microparticle and/or the nanoparticle to activate the cancer-specific T cell, and then the cancer-specific T cell is expanded and reinfused into a patient for treating cancer or preventing recurrence or metastasis. The cancer-specific T cell isolated by a sorting method has high specificity, and may prevent or treat cancer by killing cancer cells after expansion.

column12: Method for determining content of glucose in star-shaped PLGA (poly (lactic-co-glycolic acid)) and pretreatment method
column13: The invention discloses a method for determining the content of glucose in star-shaped PLGA and a pretreatment method, a mixed solution of triethylamine and methanol is adopted as a hydrolysis solvent to perform pretreatment on PLGA or PLA in a polyester compound so as to form a stable hydrolysis solution, and the hydrolysis method is adopted to rapidly extract the bonded glucose in the star-shaped PLGA, so that the content of the glucose in the star-shaped PLGA is determined. Then, HPLC-ELSD is used for detection, and the content of glucose is calculated according to the linear regression equation and the logarithm value of the glucose peak area in the chromatogram of the sample to be detected. The detection method is easy and convenient to operate, rapid in detection and high in sensitivity, quantitative detection of trace glucose in the star-shaped PLGA caused by glucose can be achieved, characterization methods and quality control methods of the quality attribute of the star-shaped PLGA are enriched, research on performance parameters of a sustained and controlled release preparation with the star-shaped PLGA as a carrier is facilitated, and the application prospect is wide. And a reference is provided for evaluating process change and quality difference of the sustained and controlled release preparation.

column13: Long acting parenteral pharmaceutical compositions comprising a therapeutically effective amount of glatiramer are provided. In particular, the present invention provides a long acting pharmaceutical composition comprising a therapeutically effective amount of glatiramer acetate in depot form suitable for administering at a medically acceptable location in a subject in need thereof. The depot form is suitable for subcutaneous or intramuscular implantation or injection.

column12: Drug delivery system for metabolism regulation of specific immune cells and preparation method and application thereof
column13: The invention discloses a drug delivery system for metabolism regulation of specific immune cells and a preparation method and application thereof.The drug delivery system is of a double-layer vesicle structure and comprises inner vesicles and outer vesicles, the inner vesicles are polymer vesicles formed by self-assembly of diblock polymers PEI-b-PLA or PEI-b-PLA, and the outer vesicles are polymer vesicles formed by self-assembly of diblock polymers PEI-b-PLA or PEI-b-PLA. The outer wall of the inner-layer vesicle is positively charged and is loaded with a therapeutic gene for immunoregulation of Arginase-1, the surface of the inner-layer vesicle is modified by an antibody targeting an MDSC cell surface marker, and a biguanide therapeutic drug is loaded in the inner-layer vesicle; the outer-layer vesicle is a liposome-like vesicle modified by angiotensin converting enzyme substrate polypeptide-PEG (Polyethylene Glycol) which is disintegrated in a targeted manner. The drug delivery system designed by the invention can effectively avoid influence on immune cells outside a focus, and further performs specific drug delivery and function regulation and control on immune cells such as immune microenvironment MDSC in the focus, so that effective immunotherapy of placental diseases becomes possible.

column12: MICROPARTICLES CONTAINING MOXIDECTIN AND SUSTAINED-RELEASE INJECTION COMPOSITION CONTAINING SAME
column13: The present invention relates to microparticles containing moxidectin, and a preparation method thereof. Unlike conventional heartworm prevention drugs that have a short half-life and thus require daily or monthly administration, moxidectin is continuously released for at least three months and thus the effect of preventing heartworms can be maintained for at least three months when the microparticles containing moxidectin are administered. In addition, microparticles which have a constant average diameter and a narrow diameter distribution are prepared so that initial over-release of moxidectin is prevented when the microparticles are administered, the release of the drug can be controlled to keep constant the concentration of moxidectin that is valid for at least three months, and foreign body sensation and pain can be reduced when the microparticles are applied in the form of an injection.

column12: CHEMOTHERAPEUTIC BIOADHESIVE PARTICLES WITH IMMUNOSTIMULATORY MOLECULES FOR CANCER TREATMENT
column13: A bioadhesive nanoparticle (BNP) for long-lasting local drug delivery to treat cancer was developed. The bioadhesive nanoparticles (BNP) are composed of biodegradable polymer such as poly(lactic acid)-hyperbranched polyglycerol (PLA-HPG), encapsulating a chemotherapeutic such as camptothecin (CPT). Nanoparticles (NPs) of PLA-HPG are non-adhesive NPs (NNPs), which are stealthy in their native state, but conversion of the vicinal diols of HPG to aldehydes confers the ability to form strong covalent bonds with amine-rich surfaces. The formulation is administered in combination with immunostimulatory molecules such as CPG and shows unexpectedly better killing of cancer cells.

column12: PREPARATION METHOD AND APPLICATION METHOD OF INJECTABLE PLA MICROSPHERES
column13: A preparation method and an application method of injectable polylactic acid (PLA) microspheres are provided, which relate to the field of biomedical technologies. column13: The present invention provides an improved process for preparing microparticles containing glatiramer acetate having low levels of residual organic solvent(s), in particular dichloromethane. The microparticles are incorporated into long acting parenteral pharmaceutical compositions in depot form that are suitable for subcutaneous or intramuscular implantation or injection, and that may be used to treat multiple sclerosis.

column12: A METHOD FOR PREPARING MICROPARTICLES FOR DRUG DELIVERY
column13: Disclosed is a method for preparing microparticles for drug delivery. The method comprises providing a mold comprising multiple individual, open compartments arranged on a first surface of the mold. The open compartments are separated from each other by one or more edges. Each edge has a width of 5 µm or less. The method comprises coating the first surface of the mold with a mold layer comprising a biocompatible and/or biodegradable material having a first release characteristic at a first condition. The method comprises coating the first surface of the mold with a top layer comprising a biocompatible and/or biodegradable material having a second release characteristic at the first condition for provision of closed microparticles in the multiple individual compartments. The method comprises separating the closed microparticles by cutting the mold layer and the top layer using the one or more edges. By cutting the mold layer and the top layer using the one or more edges discrete microparticles are provided.

column13: A cerebrovascular unit tumor (CVU-T)-on-a-chip model that models both the blood brain barrier (BBB) and tumor is described. The model provided a physiologically relevant GBM tumor model including a corresponding microenvironment complete with a BBB component that is crucial in dictating drug bioavailability to the tumor. Additionally a novel biodegradable microcapsule for sustained local delivery of a therapeutic such as a connexin hemichannel inhibitor is provided. The therapeutic sensitizes malignant GBM populations to systemic TMZ chemotherapy.

column12: Composition and method for reducing joint pain associated with hemarthrosis and hemophilic arthropathy
column13: The invention disclosed herein relates to a composition and method of reducing the joint pain associated with hemarthrosis or hemophilic arthropathy. In a preferred embodiment, rofecoxib or celecoxib can be encapsulated in PLGA micro-particles for controlled, sustained release over a 2-8-week period. The non-systemic delivery and the controlled, sustained release of rofecoxib alleviate the cardiovascular side effects associated with systemic rofecoxib treatments.

column12: TARGETING DELIVERY SYSTEM LOADED WITH WHOLE-CELL COMPONENTS AND USE THEREOF
column13: A targeting delivery system loaded with whole-cell components, which relates to the technical field of immunotherapy. The targeting delivery system is a nano-sized or micron-sized particle with a target head on the surface, and the particle is loaded with whole-cell components of cancer cells or cancer tissues; the whole-cell components are water-soluble ingredients and water-insoluble ingredients of whole cells in cells or tissues, and the water-insoluble ingredients are dissolved by a solubilizer; and the target head binds to a molecule on the surface of a specific cell or tissue, so as to help the particle to enter the cell or tissue. According to the targeting delivery system, a specific solubilizer is used to solubilize the water-insoluble part, which allows same to be dissolved in an aqueous solution, so that the whole-cell antigens of the water-soluble ingredients and the water-insoluble ingredients in cancer cells or tissues can be combined to prepare a cancer vaccine. column12: BIOLOGICAL FUNCTION COMPOSITE POROUS POLYESTER MICROSPHERES AND PREPARATION METHOD THEREFOR
column13: The present invention provides biological function composite porous polyester microspheres, the polyester forming the polyester microspheres being a mixture of polylactic acid (PLA) and poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA); the PLGA comprises one or more of PLGA, end-group modified PLGA and bonded PLGA; the end-group modified PLGA is amino or carboxyl modified PLGA; and the bonded PLGA is end-group modified PLGA which undergoes an amino or carboxyl chemical bonding method to become loaded with one or more of hyaluronic acid (HA), collagen (Col) and cytokines. The microspheres prepared in the present invention are round in shape, have a uniform particle size distribution, have high and adjustable porosity, and simultaneously have high drug loading capacity and encapsulation efficiency. The invention can achieve controllable release of bioactive molecules in an early stage, middle stage and later stage, that is, by adjusting the mass ratios of PLA and PLGA in the polyester microspheres the degradation time thereof in the body can be adjusted, for instance to 2 months, 6 months, 24 months, etc., thus bringing about biological effects at different times.

column12: Preparation process of PLA (polylactic acid) microspheres for controlled release of drugs
column13: The invention discloses a preparation process of PLA (polylactic acid) microspheres for controlled release of drugs, and belongs to the technical field of polymer microspheres. column12: Lacrimal implants and related methods
column13: Lacrimal implants and related methods providing secure, wedgable retention within a lacrimal punctum and associated canaliculus of an eye are disclosed. column12: Preparation method and application of composite hydrogel based on bioadhesive nanoparticles
column13: The invention belongs to the technical field of biological medicine, and particularly relates to a preparation method and application of composite hydrogel based on bioadhesive nanoparticles. Bioadhesive nanoparticles BNP based on PLA-HPG react with carboxymethyl chitosan, and reversible Schiff base bonds are formed through aldehyde groups on the surface of BNP and amino groups of carboxymethyl chitosan, so that BNP and macromolecules are crosslinked, and the composite hydrogel which has a porous network structure and contains the bioadhesive nanoparticles is formed. The composite hydrogel has good biocompatibility and injectability, the BNP and a porous structure in the composite hydrogel enable the hydrogel to simultaneously deliver water-insoluble and water-soluble drugs, and the composite hydrogel has a slow release effect, can be applied to abdominal cavity drug delivery, skin drug delivery and the like, greatly expands the application value of the BNP, and has a huge potential application prospect.

column12: Leuprorelin acetate sustained-release microsphere for injection as well as preparation method and application of leuprorelin acetate sustained-release microsphere
column13: The invention discloses a leuprorelin acetate sustained-release microsphere for injection as well as a preparation method and application of the leuprorelin acetate sustained-release microsphere. The method comprises the following steps: mixing leuprorelin acetate with water, adding stearic acid into the mixture for dissolving, quickly freeze-drying in liquid nitrogen, and then performing freeze-drying treatment to obtain a combination; dissolving a polylactide high-molecular polymer in an organic solvent, adding the combined body into the organic solvent, and stirring and dissolving to obtain a mixture; and carrying out spray drying on the mixture, then removing the organic solvent, adding auxiliary materials, mixing, and carrying out freeze-drying treatment to obtain the leuprorelin acetate sustained-release microspheres. The microspheres are subjected to release degree, drug loading capacity, granularity and rat testosterone experiments, the results show that the microspheres are consistent with the original leuprorelin acetate microspheres, and compared with leuprorelin high-molecular polymer PLA microspheres prepared by a multiple emulsion method, the microspheres prepared by the invention greatly improve the burst release effect of drugs, improve the recovery rate of the drugs and reduce the drug cost. Meanwhile, stable release lasts for 3 months or more, and the release degree requirement is met.

column12: INTRACAMERAL DRUG DELIVERY DEPOTS
column13: Methods of treating an eye for an ocular condition such as placing a composite depot comprising a xerogel with embedded degradable particles into an anterior chamber of an eye to deliver a therapeutic agent. The xerogel is a hydrogel after exposure to intraocular fluid and is degradable. The degradable particles comprise the therapeutic agent and hydrolytically degrade in the anterior chamber to provide a controlled release of the therapeutic agent into the eye. Materials and processes for making depots are provided as well as alternative methods of their use.

column12: Full-biodegradable plastic controlled-release fertilizer coating material and fertilizer forming process
column13: The invention discloses a full-biodegradable plastic controlled-release fertilizer coating material and a fertilizer forming process, and belongs to the field of agricultural fertilizers. The composition is characterized by comprising the following components in parts by weight: 5-99 parts of a semi-aromatic carbon dioxide-based copolymer and 1-40 parts of a regulator, the conditioning agent comprises PPC, PBAT, PCL, PLA and a pore-forming agent. The controlled-release fertilizer forming process comprises the following steps: dissolving the controlled-release fertilizer coating material into a solvent to prepare a coating solution; dipping or spraying the coating solution on the fertilizer, transferring the fertilizer into a vacuum fluidized bed for devolatilization, and curing the compound fertilizer coating material on the surface of the fertilizer. The controlled-release fertilizer coating material provided by the invention can be completely degraded into carbon dioxide and water through biological decomposition in soil, the water blocking performance is good after a coating is formed, the influence of the water content in the soil is small, the price is low, the dosage is small, and the disintegration speed can meet the slow release requirement of the fertilizer.

column12: PREPARATION OF TRIS-BNP NANOPARTICLE AND APPLICATION THEREOF IN TREATMENT OF SKIN DISEASES
column13: Provided are a preparation method for a Tris-BNP nanoparticle and an application thereof in the treatment of skin diseases, which relate to the technical field of drug carrier materials. The preparation method is as follows: preparing PLA and HPG into NNPs, oxidizing and reducing the NNPs by means of sodium periodate to then obtain bioadhesive nanoparticles (BNPs), and finally dispersing the BNPs in Tris-HCL to neutralize the bioadhesiveness thereof, so as to prepare Tris-BNPs nanoparticles. The obtained Tris-BNPs may penetrate the stratum corneum of the skin well and penetrate deep into the skin when the stratum corneum of the skin becomes loose in a disease state (e.g., psoriasis), and Tris thereon will permeate into the tissue with the Tris-BNPs and gradually spreads. Finally, the BNPs restore the bioadhesiveness thereof, so that same may stay deep in the skin, and may be used as a carrier to load drugs and applied in the treatment of skin diseases to exert a better therapeutic effect.

column12: CHEMOTHERAPEUTIC BIOADHESIVE PARTICLES WITH IMMUNOSTIMULATORY MOLECULES FOR CANCER TREATMENT
column13: A bioadhesive nanoparticle (BNP) for long-lasting local drug delivery to treat cancer was developed. The bioadhesive nanoparticles (BNP) are composed of biodegradable polymer such as poly(lactic acid)-hyperbranched polyglycerol (PLA-HPG), encapsulating a chemotherapeutic such as camptothecin (CPT). Nanoparticles (NPs) of PLA-HPG are non-adhesive NPs (NNPs), which are stealthy in their native state, but conversion of the vicinal diols of HPG to aldehydes confers the ability to form strong covalent bonds with amine-rich surfaces. The formulation is administered in combination with immunostimulatory molecules such as CPG and shows unexpectedly better killing of cancer cells.

column12: Biological functional composite porous polyester microsphere and preparation method thereof
column13: The invention provides a biological functional composite porous polyester microsphere. Polyester for forming the polyester microsphere is a mixture of polylactic acid (PLA) and polylactic acid-glycolic acid copolymer (PLGA); the PLGA is prepared from one or more of PLGA, end group modified PLGA and bonded PLGA; the end group modified PLGA is amino or carboxyl modified PLGA; the bonded PLGA is prepared by loading one or more of hyaluronic acid (HA), collagen (COL) and cell factors on end group modified PLGA through amino or carboxyl in a chemical bonding manner. The microspheres prepared by the method are round and neat in appearance, uniform in particle size distribution, high and adjustable in porosity, and high in drug loading capacity and encapsulation efficiency. The controllable release of bioactive molecules in the early stage, the middle stage and the later stage of injection can be realized, that is, the degradation time, such as 2 months, 6 months and 24 months, of the polyester microspheres in vivo is adjusted by adjusting the mass ratio of PLA to PLGA in the polyester microspheres, so that the biological effects of different time periods are exerted.

column12: Magnetically-responsive thermally-sensitive fluorescent micelle particle and preparation method therefor
column13: A magnetically-responsive thermally-sensitive fluorescent micelle particle and a preparation method therefor. In the method, N-isopropylacrylamide, N,N-dimethylacrylamide, polylactic acid, etc. are used as raw materials to synthesize a thermosensitive P(NIPAM-co-DMAM)-b-PLA triblock polymer; a dextran-magnetic lamellar composite hydroxide-fluorouracil magnetic sustained-release drug delivery system is assembled at the core of the thermosensitive micelle by simultaneous hydration and dialysis, so as to prepare a magnetically-responsive thermally-sensitive fluorescent micelle having magnetic response and temperature-sensitivity; and water-soluble near-infrared CdHgTe quantum dots (QD) are grafted onto the surface of the magnetically-responsive thermally-sensitive micelle layer using an electrostatic binding technique, so as to finally prepare DMF@TRM@QD fluorescent micellar particles having near-infrared fluorescence emission, magnetic targeting, and thermosensitive controlled-release properties. The product of the present invention features an appropriate LCST, a simple process, low costs, a high drug load, good water solubility, and high sol stability. The micellar particle has ideal thermosensitive properties, magnetic targeting properties, and fluorescent tracer functions, and has special application prospects in the fields of targeted tumor therapy and magnetically induced thermotherapy.

column13: A wound dressing including a porous biosynthetic polymer film comprising a poly(lactide-co-caprolactone) ("PLC") copolymer or other suitable polymer matrix, and a local analgesic loaded therein, to provide pain relief over an extended period of time (e.g., for 5-7 days), e.g., for healing of a partial thickness dermal injury. The preparation method comprises the following steps of: preparing NNPs from PLA and HPG; carrying out oxidation reduction on the NNPs by using sodium periodate to obtain nanoparticles BNPs with biological adhesion; and finally dispersing the BNPs in Tris-HCL to neutralize the biological viscosity of the BNPs so as to prepare the Tris-BNPs nanoparticles. When skin cuticle becomes loose in a disease state (such as psoriasis), the prepared Tris-BNPs can well permeate the skin cuticle and permeate into the deep part of the skin, Tris on the Tris-BNPs can gradually diffuse along with the Tris-BNPs permeating into tissues, and finally, the BNPs restore biological viscosity, so that the Tris-BNPs can be detained in the deep part of the skin and can be used as a carrier to load a medicine, the Tris-BNPs can be applied to treatment of skin diseases and exert a better treatment effect.

column12: MICROPARTICLES FOR CONTROLLED RELEASE OF EXTRACELLULAR VESICLES AND METHODS FOR FABRICATING THE SAME
column13: A microparticle has a core comprising an aqueous phase including (i) a bioactive material comprising an extracellular vesicle (e.g., exosome) or a material derived from a cell and (ii) an optional hydrophilic stabilizing agent. An amphiphilic layer is disposed around the core and has a biodegradable amphiphilic block copolymer comprising hydrophilic and hydrophobic domains capable of self-assembly to define a core-shell structure. An aqueous shell layer may be temporarily disposed over the amphiphilic layer. The microparticle has a diameter of ≥ about 1 ≤ about 100 micrometers and releases the bioactive material for ≥ about 6 weeks when exposed to an aqueous medium. A tissue regeneration system can be implanted in a subject and may include a biocompatible tissue reconstruction material with the controlled release microparticles distributed therein. Methods of making controlled release microparticles are also provided, which form water-in-oil-in-water emulsions that are solidified.

column12: MULTI-FUNCTIONAL ANALGESIC-RELEASING WOUND DRESSING
column13: A wound dressing including a porous biosynthetic polymer film comprising a poly(lactide-co-caprolactone) (“PLC”) copolymer or other suitable polymer matrix, and a local analgesic loaded therein, to provide pain relief over an extended period of time (e.g., for 5-7 days), e.g., for healing of a partial thickness dermal injury. The PLC copolymer may have a particular lactide/caprolactone molar ratio (e.g., from 2:1 to 9:1) to ensure slow, sustained release of the bupivacaine or other analgesic. The dressing may provide a water vapor transmission rate from 1000 g/m2·day to 3000 g/m2·day to facilitate fast healing and regrowth of new epithelial tissue beneath the dressing. The dressing is configured to remain positioned over the dermal injury, providing wound protection for about 14 days, after which is simply debrides away, falls off, or is easily and painlessly removed, once new epithelial tissue regrows.

The transparent moisture-preserving antibacterial degradable packaging film is composed of an inner active moisture-preserving layer, a transparent supporting layer and an outer barrier moisture-preserving layer which are prepared from biodegradable base materials. The inner active moisture-preserving layer takes modified polyvinyl alcohol PVA as a main body, and comprises an intelligent antibacterial compound which is prepared by carrying an antibacterial agent on a pH response type mesoporous nano-carrier. The transparent supporting layer is prepared from the following raw materials in parts by mass: 50 to 90 parts of PLA particles, 10 to 50 parts of mPPC particles, 5 to 20 parts of acetyl tributyl citrate (ATBC), 0.5 to 2 parts of chain extender ADR-4368 and 0.1 to 1 part of an antioxidant 1010; The outer barrier moisture-preserving layer takes modified polyvinyl alcohol PVA as a main body, and contains 0.5-2 parts of nano silicon dioxide SiO2 for crosslinking reinforcement. The packaging film can dynamically absorb/release moisture in the internal environment, prevents condensation, and has pH controlled-release antibacterial characteristics. Moisture among the inner layer, the middle layer and the outer layer can achieve dynamic balance, and excessive accumulation of moisture in the inner environment is avoided. The packaging film can be used for fresh keeping of fresh food and has double effects of resisting bacteria and preserving moisture.

column12: PH responsive intelligent controlled-release antibacterial degradable packaging film and preparation method and application thereof
column13: The invention discloses a pH responsive intelligent controlled-release antibacterial degradable packaging film and a preparation method and application thereof. The pH responsive intelligent controlled-release antibacterial degradable packaging film is composed of an active antibacterial layer prepared from a biodegradable base material and a blocking layer, and the active antibacterial layer contains an intelligent antibacterial compound prepared from a pH response controlled-release type mesoporous nano-zinc oxide carrying antibacterial agent; a modified and dispersed graphene oxide nanosheet layer material is contained in the blocking layer, and the biodegradable base material raw material contains PBAT raw material particles, PLA raw material particles, acetyl tributyl citrate ATBC and a chain extender ADR-4368. The pH responsive high specific surface area carrier is used for carrying the antibacterial agent, and the antibacterial agent is responsively released by sensing an internal dynamic acid environment generated by wrapped fresh food or microbial metabolism, so that the release amount of the antibacterial agent is consistent with the food fresh-keeping requirement. The packaging film can be used for preserving perishable and fresh food. The raw materials are biodegradable high polymer materials and low-molecular additives harmless to the environment, and are environment-friendly.

column12: Nanoparticle Depot For Controlled And Sustained Gene Delivery
column13: One aspect of the disclosure describes a lipid conjugated cationic molecule. Other aspects of the disclosure describes nanoparticle delivery systems and methods of making the systems are disclosed. An embodiment of the nanoparticle delivery system has sustained gene delivery properties, the nanoparticle delivery system can be synthesized using biodegradable and biocompatible polymers via self-assembly. The nanoparticle delivery system comprises a plurality of nanoparticle depots, each of which has a particle-in-particle structure, and is composed of a polymeric nanoparticle, which encapsulates cationic molecule/nucleic acid complexes, facilitating enhanced retention and prolonged release of the gene payload. The polymeric nanoparticle comprises a shell, and a nanocomplex of the cationic molecule and a polynucleotide, the nanocomplexes are distributed within the shell and/or embedded in the shell. Another embodiment of the nanoparticle delivery system has one or more nanocomplexes. The one or more nanocomplexes includes a lipid conjugated cationic molecule and a polynucleotide.

column12: Daphnoretin micelle and preparation method, content detection and application thereof
column13: The invention relates to a daphnoretin micelle and a preparation method, content detection and application thereof. The daphnoretin nano-micelle is prepared by selecting a safe and degradable material PEG-PLA, and daphnoretin is prepared into a polymer micelle so as to achieve the purposes of increasing solubility and prolonging in-vivo action time. Meanwhile, the glycyrrhetinic acid coupled PEG-PLA is used as a carrier, and the nano preparation which is loaded with daphnoretin and has the liver cancer targeting property is prepared. Through in-vitro cell research, in-vivo targeting evaluation and preliminary pharmacodynamic research on the two drug-loaded micelles, the liver targeting drug delivery performance and the anti-tumor effect of the daphnoretin nano-micelle drug system are proved, and a theoretical basis is laid for in-vivo liver cancer targeting research of daphnoretin in the future; and a new thought is provided for the development of a new daphnoretin dosage form and a novel liver cancer targeting preparation.

column12: Method for regulating and controlling morphology of beads in bead-shaped nanofibers
column13: The invention discloses a method for regulating and controlling the morphology of beads in bead-shaped nanofibers. The method comprises the following steps of dissolving a spinning solute in an organic solvent, wherein the mass-to-volume ratio of the spinning solute to the organic solvent is 6%, the spinning solute comprises one or a combination of at least two of PLGA, PLA, sodium alginate, polyglycolic acid, a lactic acid-glycolic acid copolymer, collagen, silk protein, cellulose and chitosan, and the organic solvent comprises one or a combination of at least two of chloroform, acetone and N,N-dimethylformamide; and putting the prepared spinning solution into an electrostatic spinning machine for electrostatic spinning, wherein the electric injection conditions of the electrostatic spinning machine are that the voltage is 20-30 kV, the receiving distance is 7 cm, the propelling rate of an injector is 0.5 mL/h, the environment temperature is 20-30 DEG C, and the humidity is 60-70%. According to the technical scheme, the bead-shaped nanofibers with various morphologies can be obtained, and the application range and application value of the bead-shaped nanofibers in the aspects of drug loading and drug sustained release are expanded.

For example, a drug delivery device is provided that comprises a biodegradable scaffold carrying one or more anti-cancer therapeutic agents that activate the innate immune system (e.g., STING agonists) and/or the adaptive immune system (e.g., anti-PD-1 antibodies). The compositions and devices may include a cytokine (e.g., IL-15 superagonist). The drug delivery device can be implanted in the void volume of a resected tumor to prevent tumor regrowth and tumor metastasis. Also provided are methods of making the drug delivery compositions and devices as well as kits containing materials to provide the compositions and devices.

column12: A Composition for Solubilizing Alpinumisoflavone and Uses Thereof
column13: The present invention relates to a composition for solubilizing alpinumisoflavone and a use thereof. A drug carrier composition or a composition for solubilizing alpinumisoflavone according to the present invention uses polymer micelles formed through association of mPEG-b-PLA and can effectively solubilize alpinumisoflavone. Alpinumisoflavone is a hardly soluble material, and substantially does not exist in an aqueous layer but is enclosed in the micelles and solubilized. In this manner, alpinumisoflavone which is a hardly soluble material can be dissolved in an aqueous layer and developed as an intravenous injection formulation using water. Since the intravenous injection can avoid a liver first pass effect, as compared to an oral administration formulation, to reduce undesired drug loss, and shows increased bio-availability as compared to an oral administration formulation, it is an effective administration method capable of expecting a higher effect with the same dose of drug. Therefore, development of such a formulation allows effective administration of alpinumisoflavone. In addition, the composition according to the present invention shows a controlled release effect of alpinumisoflavone in the micelles, and such an effect enables increased retention of the drug in vivo. Further, the composition according to the present invention shows no toxicity, and has an advantage in that it can reduce the toxicity caused by an excipient by using a polymer.

column12: Magnetically-responsive thermally-sensitive fluorescent micelle particle and preparation method therefor
column13: A magnetically-responsive thermally-sensitive fluorescent micelle particle and a preparation method therefor. In the method, N-isopropylacrylamide, N,N-dimethylacrylamide, polylactic acid, etc. are used as raw materials to synthesize a thermosensitive P(NIPAM-co-DMAM)-b-PLA triblock polymer; a dextran-magnetic lamellar composite hydroxide-fluorouracil magnetic sustained-release drug delivery system is assembled at the core of the thermosensitive micelle by simultaneous hydration and dialysis, so as to prepare a magnetically-responsive thermally-sensitive fluorescent micelle having magnetic response and temperature-sensitivity; and water-soluble near-infrared CdHgTe quantum dots (QD) are grafted onto the surface of the magnetically-responsive thermally-sensitive micelle layer using an electrostatic binding technique, so as to finally prepare DMF@TRM@QD fluorescent micellar particles having near-infrared fluorescence emission, magnetic targeting, and thermosensitive controlled-release properties. The product of the present invention features an appropriate LCST, a simple process, low costs, a high drug load, good water solubility, and high sol stability. The micellar particle has ideal thermosensitive properties, magnetic targeting properties, and fluorescent tracer functions, and has special application prospects in the fields of targeted tumor therapy and magnetically induced thermotherapy.

column12: OXYGEN-RELEASING BIOMATERIALS, ARTICLES AND METHODS
column13: An oxygen-releasing biomaterial, articles and methods, and more particularly an oxygen-releasing biomaterial with sustained oxygen-releasing properties of four to five weeks, which is suitable for tissue engineering scaffolds, is disclosed. The biomaterial contains a hydrogel with a plurality of microparticles suspended in the hydrogel. The microparticles contain an oxygen carrier that is encapsulated in a biocompatible hydrophobic material, where the release of oxygen from the oxygen carrier is sustained over a four to five week period. The biomaterial has application in tissue engineering, osteogenesis, burn and wound treatment, and treatment of cardiac conditions, and has further antimicrobial properties.

column12: Injectable composite carrier with sustained and controlled release drug effect, composition and preparation method
column13: The invention discloses an injectable composite carrier with a sustained and controlled release drug effect, a composition and a preparation method. column12: Camptothecin compound nano drug loading system and preparation method thereof
column13: The invention provides a camptothecin compound nano drug delivery system, and solves the defects of low utilization rate, serious loss and unobvious poisoning effect on pests during application of a traditional preparation. The preparation method comprises the following steps: dissolving polylactic acid (PLA) and a camptothecin compound in an organic solvent to form an oil phase; adding polyvinylalcohol (PVA) into water, dissolving to form a PVA water solution; adding the oil phase into the PVA water solution, emulsifying to form a colloidal solution; adding a polyethylene glycol water solution into the colloidal solution, then adding a polyphenol compound water solution; volatilizing the organic solvent, centrifuging, saving the precipitate, and carrying out freeze-drying to obtain the polylactic acid-camptothecin nano drug loading system.

column12: MICROSPHERICAL SUSTAINED-RELEASE INJECTION CONTAINING ESCITALOPRAM AND METHOD FOR PREPARING SAME
column13: The present invention relates to a biodegradable polymer microsphere-containing sustained-release injection containing escitalopram as an active ingredient, and to a method for manufacturing the same. In the case of escitalopram microspheres, there is a problem of low encapsulation rate, fracture due to weak strength, and initial over-release due to the phase separation of the liquid drug and the polymer inside the microspheres. In order to solve the problem, it is possible to maximize the encapsulation amount and the encapsulation efficiency of the escitalopram adding a hydrophobic solidifying agent to uniformize the non-uniform phase, to overcome the cracking of the microspheres at high loading conditions, and to properly control the initial release and release delay of the microspheres.

column12: Celecoxib micelle-honokiol micelle drug-combined controlled-release system and preparation method thereof
column13: The invention relates to a celecoxib micelle-honokiol micelle drug-combined controlled-release system and a preparation method thereof. The drug-combined controlled-release system comprises celecoxibmicelles and honokiol micelles, wherein carrier materials of the micelles are mPEG-PLA and vitamin E-TPGS. The preparation method comprises the steps of: adequately dissolving the mPEG-PLA, the vitamin E-TPGS, celecoxib or honokiol into an organic solvent, removing the organic solvent to form a film, adding the film deionized water for hydration so as to obtain the celecoxib micelles and the honokiol micelles, and mixing the celecoxib micelles with the honokiol micelles, so as to obtain the drug-combined controlled-release system. The prepared drug-combined controlled-release system has good water solubility and an obvious controlled-release effect and is capable of reducing toxic and side effects generated during treatment of anticancer drugs, the administration dosage is reduced, and anintegral anti-tumor treatment effect is further improved.

column12: Composite membrane carrying bioactive factors PLA/PLGA/CS and preparation method thereof
column13: The invention discloses a composite membrane carrying bioactive factors PLA/PLGA/CS and a preparation method thereof. The mode of combining electrostatic spinning and electrostatic spraying is utilized, a PLA membrane is taken as a sealing layer, the diffusion of drugs can be prevented by utilizing the compactness of the PLA membrane, and mechanical support is provided; PLGA microspheres are takenas a sandwich layer to carry the drugs; and the large porosity and high biocompatibility of a CS membrane are utilized as a controlled-release layer to directly contact with damaged areas, and the purposes of neural restoration can be achieved by planning seed cells can be achieved, so that the PLA/PLGA/CS composite membrane with membrane/ball/membrane structures can be prepared. The composite membrane is stable in structure and has a certain mechanical strength, the tensile strength is 2.83+/-0.31 Mpa, and the elongation at break is 53.25+/-0.18%; the composite membrane can well carry the drugs and has good drug sustained-release effects, and the releasing of the drugs can achieve more than two months, so that the time required by the repairing of spinal cord injury can be met; and the composite membrane has no cytotoxicity and can successfully induce PC-12 cells to differentiate into neurons within 5 days, so that the composite membrane is good for neural restoration.

column12: FLOATABLE PHARMACEUTICAL MICROCAPSULE COMPOSITION
column13: Disclosed herein is a sustained release hollow core-shell microcapsule formulation for drug delivery comprising a hollow shell of one or more hydrophobic polymers, a drug containing hydrophilic or amphiphilic carrier matrix that is distributed over the inner surface of the hollow shell, a flotation agent, and an optional osmotic agent, wherein the microcapsule is capable of floating in a simulated digestive fluid for a period of from 24 to 96 hours. The microcapsules are prepared by a modified double emulsion (water/oil/water) solvent evaporation method. The microcapsule formulation may provide a sustained-release delivery system for treating chronic diseases such as Parkinson's disease, diabetes and tuberculosis, all of which require multiple drug combination therapies. The aim is to reduce dosing frequency and pill burden, thus improving patient medication compliance. In a specific embodiment, the hollow shell is formed from a mixture of Poly-L-lactide (PLLA) and poly(E-caprolactone) (PCL); and the amphiphilic carrier matrix is casein.

column12: OCULAR THERAPY USING ALPHA-2 ADRENERGIC RECEPTOR AGONISTS HAVING ENHANCED ANTERIOR CLEARANCE RATES
column13: Ophthalmically therapeutic materials, such as liquid-containing compositions and polymeric drug delivery systems, include a therapeutic component which includes an alpha 2 adrenergic receptor agonist that is cleared from the anterior segment of an individual's eye to which the material is administered. The alpha 2 adrenergic receptor agonist may have a vitreal half-life greater than about three hours. The present materials are effective in treating an ocular condition(s) that affect the anterior segment of an eye, or the anterior and posterior segment of the eye. The materials are suitable for intravitreal or periocular administration and can provide prolonged drug delivery and therapeutic benefits to patients to which the materials have been administered. The alpha 2 adrenergic receptor agonists can be provided in liquid-containing formulations and/or bioerodible and/or non-bioerodible polymeric implants and microparticles. Methods of making and using the present materials are also described.

column12: Preparation method of polylactic acid nano microspheres
column13: The invention discloses a preparation method of polylactic acid nano microspheres. The method comprises the following steps: adding PLA into dichloromethane to form an organic phase; adding a surfactant Tween20 into ultrapure water, and performing heating, stirring and dissolving at 44-46 DEG C to obtain a water phase; slowly dropwise adding the organic phase into the water phase under a stirringcondition, performing ultrasonic emulsification for 15-25 minutes after uniform stirring, performing magnetic stirring at 25-35 DEG C for 23-25 hours to completely volatilize an organic solvent, centrifugally collecting microspheres, repeatedly washing the microspheres with ultrapure water to remove the surfactant, and performing vacuum freeze drying to obtain the product. The method is simple, convenient, quick and easy to operate. The prepared polylactic acid nano microspheres have good dispersibility and balling property, and can be used as a carrier to realize targeted controlled release of drugs.

column13: A magnetically-responsive thermally-sensitive fluorescent micelle particle and a preparation method therefor. The product of the present invention features an appropriate LCST, a simple process, low costs, a high drug load, good water solubility, and high sol stability. column12: Nanolipogel vehicles for controlled delivery of different pharmaceutical agents
column13: A “nanolipogel” is a delivery vehicle including one or more lipid layer surrounding a hydrogel core, which may include an absorbent such as a cyclodextrin or ion-exchange resin. Nanolipogels can be constructed so as to incorporate a variety of different chemical entities that can subsequently be released in a controlled fashion. These different incorporated chemical entities can differ dramatically with respect to size and composition. Nanolipogels have been constructed to contain co-encapsulated proteins as well as small hydrophobic drugs within the interior of the lipid bilayer. Agents incorporated within nanolipogels can be released into the milieu in a controlled fashion, for example, nanolipogels provide a means of achieving simultaneous sustained release of agents that differ widely in chemical composition and molecular weight. Additionally, nanolipogels can favorably modulate biodistribution.

column12: Drug-coated balloon
column13: Described here are devices, systems, and methods for treating conditions or diseases of the nose, ear, or throat with an expandable device having a drug coating. The expandable devices may be delivered to a body cavity in a low-profile configuration and expanded to contact surrounding tissue. The expandable devices may deliver or release the drug coating to the tissue. Multiple expansions of a single device may be employed during treatment. Various coating excipients and manufacturing parameters for the expandable devices may also be adjusted to enhance or slow transfer of the drug coating and/or release of the drug to the target tissue site. The drug transferred to the tissue may act as an in situ depot that enables maintenance of a therapeutic level of locally delivered drug for a desired time period after removal of the expandable devices.

column12: Drug sustained-release device for cervical HPV infection
column13: The invention belongs to the field of tumor drug therapy equipment, and discloses a drug sustained-release device for cervical HPV infection. The device comprises a drug loading device and a drug delivery device; the drug loading device comprises a three-fork type base body center located in the center of the drug loading device, the three ends of the base body center are connected to a pluralityof drug loading bags respectively, and the end of the drug loading bag at the utmost end is sleeved with an end cap; an anti-HPV infection medicine is contained in the drug loading bag, a PLA wrappinglayer is arranged outside the anti-HPV infection medicine, and a PLC isolation layer is arranged on the peripheral side of the PLA wrapping layer; the center of the three-fork type base body comprises a vertical fork part and two horizontal fork parts, and a triangular groove is formed in the upper surface of the joint of the two horizontal fork parts; and the drug delivery device comprises a columnar shell, a push rod is arranged in the shell in a sliding mode, a cavity defined by the top face of the push rod and the shell is a drug delivery device installation chamber, a handle located outside the shell is arranged at the bottom of the push rod, and a columnar clamping groove with a notch in the side edge is formed outside the push rod. The device can realize slow release in the uterusof a human body, and achieves the purpose of continuous medication within a long period of time.

column12: Method for preparing bubble type hollow drug-delivery micro-needle through tip dissolving method

column12: VEHICLES FOR CONTROLLED DELIVERY OF DIFFERENT PHARMACEUTICAL AGENTS
column13: A "nanolipogel" is a delivery vehicle including one or more lipid layer surrounding a hydrogel core, which may include an absorbent such as a cyclodextrin or ion-exchange resin. Nanolipogels can be constructed so as to incorporate a variety of different chemical entities that can subsequently be released in a controlled fashion. These different incorporated chemical entities can differ dramatically with respect to size and composition. Nanolipogels have been constructed to contain co-encapsulated proteins as well as small hydrophobic drugs within the interior of the lipid bilayer. Agents incorporated within nanolipogels can be released into the milieu in a controlled fashion, for example, nanolipogels provide a means of achieving simultaneous sustained release of agents that differ widely in chemical composition and molecular weight. Additionally, nanolipogels can favorably modulate biodistribution.

column13: An injectable drug delivery device includes a core containing one or more drugs and one or more polymers. The degradable TAXOL-(P3/4HB-PCL)-PU nano-biliary stent is formed by a special soluble core-shaft-assisted coaxial electrospinning technology. column12: FLOATABLE PHARMACEUTICAL MICROCAPSULE COMPOSITION
column13: Disclosed herein is a sustained release hollow core-shell microcapsule formulation for drug delivery comprising a hollow shell of one or more hydrophobic polymers, a drug containing hydrophilic or amphiphilic carrier matrix that is distributed over the inner surface of the hollow shell, a flotation agent, and an optional osmotic agent, wherein the microcapsule is capable of floating in a simulated digestive fluid for a period of from 24 to 96 hours. The microcapsules are prepared by a modified double emulsion (water/oil/water) solvent evaporation method. The microcapsule formulation may provide a sustained-release delivery system for treating chronic diseases such as Parkinson's disease, diabetes and tuberculosis, all of which require multiple drug combination therapies. The aim is to reduce dosing frequency and pill burden, thus improving patient medication compliance. In a specific embodiment, the hollow shell is formed from a mixture of Poly-L-lactide (PLLA) and poly(E-caprolactone) (PCL); and the amphiphilic carrier matrix is casein.

column12: Chain crystallization control-based temperature-sensitive polymer material and preparation method thereof
column13: The invention relates to the field of functional high polymer materials, and aims at providing a chain crystallization control-based temperature-sensitive polymer material and a preparation method thereof. The polymer material is mixture aqueous solution of a component A and a component B, wherein the component A is monomethoxy polyethylene glycol (meth) acrylate-co-poly-l-lactic acid; the component B is monomethoxy polyethylene glycol (meth) acrylate-Co-poly-r-lactic acid; the component A and the component B are comb-shaped amphiphilic copolymers which are enantiomers of each other; and the phase transition temperature of the temperature-sensitive polymer material can be adjusted by changing a blending ratio of the two components. The preparation method is simple and can be highly implemented. A used OEGMA or OEGA unit is temperature sensitive, and the temperature sensitivity of the polymer is adjusted by regulating a crystallization structure of a PLA chain segment, so that the method is novel and the application range is expanded. The polymer material can be self-assembled in water and is both biodegradable and biocompatible, so that the polymer material has wide application inthe fields of drug controlled release carriers, soft tissue engineering scaffold materials, biosensors and the like.

column12: Taxane derivative TM-2 micellar injection, preparation method thereof and application thereof
column13: The invention provides a taxane derivative TM-2 micellar injection, a preparation method thereof and an application thereof. column12: Magneto-thermo dual-sensitive fluorescent glue beammicelle particle and preparation method thereof
column13: The invention relates to a magneto-thermo dual-sensitive fluorescent glue beammicelle particle and a preparation method thereof. The method comprises the following steps: synthesizing a thermosensitive P(NIPAM-co-DMAM)-b-PLA triblock copolymer by taking N-isopropylacrylamide, N,N-dimethylacrylamide and polylactic acid as raw materials, then assembling a dextran-magnetic lamellar compound hydroxide-fluorouracil magnetic sustained and controlled release drug delivery system to a core of a thermosensitive glue beammicelle through a synchronous hydration and dialysis method so as to prepare a magneto-thermo dual-sensitive fluorescent glue beammicelle with magnetic response and temperature sensitivity, then grafting water-soluble near-infrared CdHgTe quantum dots (QD) on the surface of a magneto-thermo dual-sensitive thermosensitive glue beammicelle layer by using an electrostatic bonding technique, and finally preparing a DMF@TRM@QD fluorescent glue beammicelle particle with near-infraredfluorescence emission, magnetic targeting and thermosensitive controlled-release properties. The magneto-thermo dual-sensitive fluorescent glue beammicelle particle has appropriate low critical solution temperature (LCST ), is simple in process, low in cost, high in drug loading capacity, excellent in water solubility and high in sol stability, has a desirable thermosensitive property, magnetic targeting property and fluorescence tracing function, and has special application prospects in the fields of targetinged therapy and magneto-thermal therapy of tumors.

column12: Pesticide sustained release microsphere and preparation method thereof
column13: The invention aims to disclose a pesticide sustained release microsphere and a preparation method thereof. The pesticide sustained release microsphere is composed of a core material and a wall material, wherein a mass ratio of the core material to the wall material is 1 to 1-6. The pesticide sustained release microsphere is characterized in that the wall material is prepared from polylactic acid (PLA) and poly(butylene succinate) (PBS) in a mass ratio of 1 to 1-9; the core material is prepared from two pesticide active compounds. By the use of the characteristic of high curing rate in an emulsification process, the PLA is mixed with the PBS to prepare the wall material to increase the settling rate in an emulsifying shear process, so that the encapsulation efficiency of a drug is effectively improved; furthermore, after the PLA and the PBS are mixed, the number of holes in the surface of the microsphere can be effectively decreased, and the drug release time is prolonged. The pesticidesustained release microsphere disclosed by the invention is uniform in particle size and regular in shape; the encapsulation efficiency of the pesticide active compounds is over 70 percent, and the drug release time lasts for 25 days or longer; furthermore, after the drug is completely released, the wall material can be biologically degraded without causing pollution.

column12: POLYMER-BASED THERAPEUTICS FOR INDUCTIVE BROWNING OF FAT
column13: This disclosure features the methods and compositions involving development of novel polymer-based therapeutics that induce browning of white adipocytes for the treatment of obesity and its associated metabolic diseases. The therapeutic effects are largely attributed to the promotion of brown and/or beige adipocyte development and function by leveraging adipocyte plasticity and polymer-based drug delivery systems. Both brown and beige adipocytes are densely packed with mitochondria which highly express uncoupling protein-1 (UCP1), a thermogenic protein mediating non-shivering thermogenesis.

column12: Triadimefon*propiconazole polylactic acid microsphere and preparation method thereof
column13: The invention discloses a triadimefon*propiconazole polylactic acid microsphere and a preparation method thereof. The method comprises the following steps: taking a triadimefon*propiconazole compoundmedicine as a core material, taking a biodegradable material polylactic acid (PLA) as a wall material, and preparing the triadimefon*propiconazole polylactic acid sustained release microsphere by an emulsion-solvent evaporation method. The influence of each experimental factor on the microsphere preparation process is investigated by a single factor, and with the adoption of an orthogonal experiment, the preparation process is further optimized. The optimal process conditions of the microsphere are screened as follows: the mass ratio of the core material to the wall material is 1:3, the mass fraction of the emulsifier is 1.50%, the volume ratio of oil and water phases is 1:20, the polylactic acid concentration is 120 mg/mL, the high-speed dispersion time is 0.6min, the high-speed dispersion speed is 4000 revolutions per minute, the magnetic stirring time is 3 hours, and the magnetic stirring speed is 600 revolutions per minute.

column12: Biodegradable material loaded pesticide microsphere suspending agent and preparation method thereof
column13: The invention relates to a biodegradable material loaded pesticide microsphere suspending agent and a preparation method thereof. The preparation method is characterized in that the commixture of biodegradable polypropylene carbonate PPC and polylactic acid PLA is used as the wall material to prepare emamectin benzoate sustained-release microspheres, and a wetting dispersant, a thickening agent, an anti-freezing agent and water are added to service as the auxiliary materials to prepare the emamectin benzoate microsphere suspending agent. The emamectin benzoate microsphere suspending agent comprises, 45-120g/L of emamectin benzoate microspheres, 35-60g/L of wetting dispersant, 2.4-5g/L of thickening agent aluminum-magnesium silicate and sodium alginate, 25-50g/L of anti-freezing agent ethylene glycol and the balance water. The suspending agent and the preparation method thereof have the advantages that the cost of the compound wall material used by the suspending agent is lowered, the environment friendliness of the compound wall material is increased, the compound wall material can be naturally biodegraded into carbon dioxide and water after the suspending agent is applied to fields, the compound wall material is good in environment compatibility, and harm, caused by the heavy use of non-degraded wall materials such as polyurea, to environments is reduced.

column12: INJECTABLE AND BIODEGRADABLE POLYMER FORMULATIONS FOR CONTROLLED RELEASE OF BIOLIGIC AGENTS
column13: The present disclosure is directed to injectable formulations that include biodegradable polymers based on trimethylene carbonate (TMC) with mole fractions of polylactic acid (PLA) and/or polyglycolic acid (PGA) that are used to deliver a bioactive agent to a targeted site. Excipients such as polyethylene glycol (PEG) may be added to the formulations to reduce the injection force and/or to modulate the release of the bioactive agent. Suitable biodegradable polymers for use in the injectable formulations include D,L-PLA:TMC, D-PLA:TMC, L-PLA:TMC, TMC:PLA:PGA and variations thereof. Additionally, copolymers of TMC and PLA and terpolymers of TMC:PLA:PGA may be formed into nanoparticles and delivered to the target site with an injectable crosslinkable polyethylene glycol system. In at least one embodiment, the injectable formulations are used to treat ocular diseases.

column12: BIODEGRADING IMPLANTABLE OCULAR SUSTAINED RELEASE DRUG DELIVERY SYSTEM
column13: An ocular implant is provided for an intraocular delivery of a therapeutic biologic agent. The implant may be used intracamerally or intravitreally. The implant may include a sustained-release biodegradable core and a biodegradable shell, wherein the shell has a longer biodegradable half-life than the core. The core may include a biodegradable gel medium, an active therapeutic biologic agent, and a biologic stabilizer. Upon insertion into the anterior chamber or vitreous body of an eye, the therapeutic biologic agent is released over an extended period, that may range from one day to one year. The therapeutic biologic agent may be, for example, tissue-plasminogen activator, an anti-VEGF agent, or another biopharmaceutical. The biodegradable implant may completely dissolve after implantation and need not be removed.

column12: Vehicles For Controlled Delivery of Different Pharmaceutical Agents
column13: A “nanolipogel” is a delivery vehicle including one or more lipid layer surrounding a hydrogel core, which may include an absorbent such as a cyclodextrin or ion-exchange resin. Nanolipogels can be constructed so as to incorporate a variety of different chemical entities that can subsequently be released in a controlled fashion. These different incorporated chemical entities can differ dramatically with respect to size and composition. Nanolipogels have been constructed to contain co-encapsulated proteins as well as small hydrophobic drugs within the interior of the lipid bilayer. Agents incorporated within nanolipogels can be released into the milieu in a controlled fashion, for example, nanolipogels provide a means of achieving simultaneous sustained release of agents that differ widely in chemical composition and molecular weight. Additionally, nanolipogels can favorably modulate biodistribution.

column12: METHODS OF DELIVERING A NEUROPROTECTIVE POLYPEPTIDE TO THE CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM
column13: The present disclosure provides a method for delivering a neuroprotective polypeptide to at least a portion of a central nervous system (CNS) of a subject. The method includes administering to the systemic blood circulation of the subject a therapeutically effective amount of a neuroprotective polypeptide by a controlled-release formulation or a device providing a sustained release of the neuroprotective polypeptide including at least one neuroprotective polypeptide selected from the group consisting of GLP-1, exendin-4, or a therapeutically effective GLP-1 or exendin-4 analogue; the neuroprotective polypeptide binds to and activates a receptor that binds at least one of GLP-1, exendin-4, or a combination thereof; and the controlled-release neuroprotective formulation or the sustained release of the neuroprotective polypeptide enhances the delivery of the neuroprotective polypeptide across a blood-brain barrier (BBB) of the subject to at least a portion of the CNS relative to a rapid release formulation of the neuroprotective polypeptide. Also disclosed is a method of treating a subject with a CNS-related disease or reducing at least one symptom of a CNS-related disease in a subject in need thereof.

column12: AN ANTI BIOTIC LOADED BIODEGRADABLE DRUG DELIVERY SYSTEM FOR TARGETTING PERIODONTAL INFECTIONS AND PERI-IMPLANT DISEASES
column13: The embodiments herein disclose method of synthesizing a composition of controlled drug (antibiotics) release for the treatment of peri-implantitis and periodontal infections which damages the Osseo-integrated dental implant and generates a loss of supporting bone. The combination of metronidazole and amoxicillin overcomes a wide range of pathogens associated with peri-implantitis. A localized biodegradable controlled drug delivery composition is synthesized for treatment of dental and implants infections (peri-implantisis). The system comprises polymer and antibiotics (metronidazole and amoxicillin). The system burst releases antibiotics in the first hours after administration, followed by a controlled release of the antibiotics for a time period up of 3 weeks. The antibiotic concentration is maintained in a suitable therapeutic range. An analysis after 14 days illustrates the elimination of the bacterial biofilm and bactericidal property of the composition.

column12: DRUG DELIVERY COMPOSITIONS AND USES THEREOF
column13: Provided are drug delivery compositions and devices useful for the treatment and/or prevention of cancer and metastatic tumors. For example, a drug delivery device is provided that comprises a biodegradable scaffold carrying one or more anti-cancer therapeutic agents that activate the innate immune system (e.g., STING agonists) and/or the adaptive immune system (e.g., anti-PD-1 antibodies). The compositions and devices may include a cytokine (e.g., IL- 15 superagonist). The drug delivery device can be implanted in the void volume of a resected tumor to prevent tumor regrowth and tumor metastasis. Also provided are methods of making the drug delivery compositions and devices as well as kits containing materials to provide the compositions and devices.

column12: DRUG ELUTING STENT AND METHOD OF USE OF THE SAME FOR ENABLING RESTORATION OF FUNCTIONAL ENDOTHELIAL CELL LAYERS
column13: The present disclosure relates to drug eluting stents, methods of making, using, and verifying long-term stability of the drug eluting stents, and methods for predicting long term stent efficacy and patient safety after implantation of a drug eluting stent. In one embodiment, a drug eluting stent may include a stent framework; a drug-containing layer; a drug embedded in the drug-containing layer; and a biocompatible base layer disposed over the stent framework and supporting the drug-containing layer. The drug-containing layer may have an uneven coating thickness. In addition or in alternative, the drug-containing layer may be configured to significantly dissolve/dissipate/disappear between 45 days and 60 days after stent implantation. Stents of the present disclosure may reduce, minimize, or eliminate patient risks associated with the implantation of a stent, including, for example, restenosis, thrombosis, and/or MACE.

column12: COMPOSITIONS AND METHODS OF TUMOR TREATMENT UTILIZING NANOPARTICLES
column13: The present invention is directed to a method for treating cancer intraperitoneally in a subject. The method comprises administering to said subject in need thereof an anti-cancer agent encapsulated in nanoparticles wherein nanoparticles are characterized to slowly release anti-cancer agent in a timely fashion that allows efficient killing of tumor cells. The nanoparticles described herein are characterized to slowly release anti-cancer agent at a rate of 30% or less per 24 hours based on in vitro drug dissolution study.

column12: Intraocular drug delivery device and associated methods
column13: An intraocular active agent delivery device can include an active agent homogenously combined with a biodegradable active agent matrix such that the entire delivery device is homogenous. The homogenous delivery device can have a shape and size to fit within a lens capsule or ciliary sulcus of an eye and provide a therapeutically effective amount of the active agent to the eye. The biodegradable active agent matrix can be formulated to provide sustained release of the therapeutically effective amount of the active agent during a release period. In some examples, the active agent can include dexamethasone.

column12: Mucoadhesive nanoparticle composition comprising immunosuppresant and methods of use thereof
column13: Disclosed is a mucoadhesive nanoparticle delivery system for delivering an immunosuppressant, such as cyclosporine A, to a mucosal site for treatment of a disease or condition involving inflammation or excess immune activity. The system comprises nanoparticles formed from a plurality of linear amphiphilic block copolymers, each having a hydrophobic block comprising polylactide (PLA) and a hydrophilic block comprising dextran. The nanoparticles are surface-functionalized with a mucosal targeting moiety, such as a phenylboronic acid derivative, for targeted delivery and enhanced retention at the mucosal site. Pharmaceutical compositions, methods, and uses thereof comprising the mucoadhesive nanoparticle delivery system are disclosed. The compositions can be administered in an effective amount for treating the disease or condition while substantially preserving or restoring the function and/or integrity of the mucosal lining. The composition may be formulated as an aqueous suspension for administration to an anterior surface of the eye in the treatment of dry eye syndrome.

column12: Hydrogel encapsulated cells and anti-inflammatory drugs
column13: A composition containing biocompatible hydrogel encapsulating mammalian cells and anti-inflammatory drugs is disclosed. The encapsulated cells have reduced fibrotic overgrowth after implantation in a subject. The compositions contain a biocompatible hydrogel having encapsulated therein mammalian cells and anti-inflammatory drugs or polymeric particles loaded with anti-inflammatory drugs. The anti-inflammatory drugs are released from the composition after transplantation in an amount effective to inhibit fibrosis of the composition for at least ten days. Methods for identifying and selecting suitable anti-inflammatory drug-loaded particles to prevent fibrosis of encapsulated cells are also described. Methods of treating a disease in a subject are also disclosed that involve administering a therapeutically effective amount of the disclosed encapsulated cells to the subject.

The resulting, inventive retinol/aCa-polyP nano- or microspheres fiber mats show antimicrobial and wound healing properties and was found to increase the expression of the genes encoding for leptin and the leptin receptor, as well as the fatty acid binding protein 4 (FABP4) in a synergistic manner. column13: A pH responsive and mucoadhesive pharmaceutical dosage form for the release of a pharmaceutically active agent is described. The different membranous layers perform different functions in order to create a drug delivery system which is able to deliver a drug to a specific site, for a particular period of time and with a specific drug release pattern. The dosage form can have two or more intermediate layers, each layer comprising an active agent. The mucoadhesive layer can also include an active agents. The dosage form is preferably an oral or buccal delivery form for release of the active agent into the gastro intestinal tract. The intermediate layer can be an electrospun fibrous membrane layer containing the active agent.

column12: Preparation of polyoxometallate supported anticancer nanometer preparation
column13: The invention discloses a polyoxometallate supported anticancer nanometer preparation and a preparation method thereof. The used polyoxometallates (POMs) are novel inorganic materials and have huge potential in treatment application of cancers. However, since the POMs are low in water solubility and unstable in an aqueous phase, the application of the POMs in the anticancer field is limited. The preparation method disclosed by the invention comprises the following steps: coating materials (PLA-PEG2000, TPGS-COOH) with biocompatibility so as to prepare a nano-carrier; modifying the surface of the nano-carrier by utilizing targeted molecular folic acid, and finally preparing the polyoxometallate supported anticancer nanometer preparation with the functions of in-vivo long circulation, active targeting, high curative effects, small toxic and side effects, high stability and the like. The polyoxometallate supported anticancer nanometer preparation is expected to fully achieve effects in the cancer treatment field. The polyoxometallate supported anticancer nanometer preparation disclosed by the invention provides a novel thought for development of a nano drug delivery system for treating cancers and has great theoretical research significances and potential application values.

column12: LONGLIFE PACKAGING
column13: Spoilage resistant packaging includes one or more anti-spoilage agents in the form of an anti-microbial agent in an amount effective to prevent or reduce the chance of spoilage of an item stored in the packaging due to microorganisms. A preferred form of the anti-microbial agent is a composition containing silver or a silver component, such as silver compound. In one form the silver compound is, an inorganic salt of silver, optionally combined together with another metal or other anti-microbial agent. An effective dosage of the anti-microbial agent is incorporated into the material from which the packaging is manufactured so as to either contact directly the item being stored in the packaging or be released to the atmosphere or environment within the packaging to counteract the effects of spoilage of the item by microorganisms. The advantage of using the anti-microbial agent is that the shelf life of the item stored in the packaging is extended whilst preserving the qualities of the item, such as the organoleptic qualities, appearance and similar.

According to the system and the preparation method, the photosensitizer, namely, pyrophaeophorbide-a (PPA) is bonded to two ends of the copolymer, namely, hydroxylated-polylactic acid-polyglycolic acid (HO-PLA-PEG-PLA-OH) through a chemical bonding method, thus the product, namely, the photosensitizer-embedded polylactic acid-polyglycolic acid polymer (PPA-PLA-PEG-PLA-PPA) is obtained, then the chemotherapy medicine, namely, paclitaxel is encapsulated physically by adopting an emulsified solvent evaporation method, thus the binary-drug-loading nanometer delivery release system (PPA NP-PTX) is prepared, then F3 peptide with the specific targeting function and the cell penetrating function is modified on the surface of the system, and thus the photodynamic therapy and chemotherapy combined drug delivery nanometer delivery release system with the binary targeting property is prepared. The experiment proves that the delivery system has the strong lethal effect for drug resistant tumor cells, has the obvious in-vivo tumor targeting effect, and has the obvious treatment effect for the mice bearing the multidrug resistant tumor, and thus the combined drug delivery nanometer system has the clinical application prospect.

column12: Embeddable micro-needle patch for transdermal drug delivery and method of manufacturing the same
column13: An embeddable micro-needle patch for transdermal drug delivery and method of manufacturing the same are disclosed. The embeddable micro-needle patch for transdermal drug delivery comprises a supporting substrate, on which the surface includes a plurality of extruded supporting shafts; a biodegradable carrier, which is formed of biodegradable polymer material and disposed on the supporting shaft; and drugs, which are encapsulated in the biodegradable carrier. When the embeddable micro-needle patch for transdermal drug delivery is attached to the skin for a predetermined time, the biodegradable carrier is separated from the supporting shafts and embedded into the skin, and the biodegradable carrier may swell and then degrade, so as to release the drugs, which are encapsulated in the biodegradable carrier, at a rate of 1%-99% loaded drug per day into the skin. Accordingly, velocity of releasing the drugs may be regulated, so as to sustain the drug efficacy.
